title: Dinesh Sharma v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
disposition: Section 482 CrPC application dismissed; s.135 prosecution not quashed.
headnote: Payment of electricity dues does not obliterate an offence under s.135 of the Electricity Act, 2003. Compounding is at the department's instance; the accused cannot compel it. A High Court order on recovery under Electricity Supply Code, 2005 clause 8.1 has no application in a criminal matter. The 482 challenge to the sessions court's 30.7.2010 order in Special Case No. 514 of 2008 was dismissed.
facts: Dinesh Sharma faced Special Case No. 514 of 2008 (State versus Dinesh) before the Additional Sessions Judge-Ist, Gautam Budh Nagar, arising from Crime No. 396 of 2008 under section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 at P.S. Sector-58, Noida. Challenging the sessions court's order dated 30 July 2010, he moved the High Court under section 482 CrPC, relying on payment of electricity dues and a photocopy of an Allahabad High Court order in Misc. Petition No. 31705 of 2009, a recovery matter under clause 8.1 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

reusable_constructions.construction: Payment of electricity dues, even in full with charges, does not obliterate an offence under s.135 of the Electricity Act, 2003; criminal prosecution is independent of civil recovery.
Compounding of an Electricity Act offence is at the department's instance; the accused cannot compel the licensee to compound.

holding_units.topic: payment of dues does not obliterate theft prosecution
holding_units.holding: Prosecution of a crime is a different matter from payment of electricity dues. Mere payment of dues does not obliterate an offence under s.135 of the Electricity Act, 2003: crime is against society. Compounding can be done only by the department if it so desires; the accused cannot compel compounding. Even payment of the entire dues with electricity charges leaves the accused liable to prosecution under s.135. A judgment in Misc. Petition No. 31705 of 2009 on recovery under Electricity Supply Code, 2005 clause 8.1 has no application in a criminal matter. The 482 application to quash the order dated 30.7.2010 in Special Case No. 514 of 2008 was dismissed as bereft of merit.
